title: How does vaping affect your singing voice?
description:
“It’s so stupid and it changed my voice”- that’s what Selena Gomez recently said about vaping nicotine. She’s now stopped, but what could the long term affects be for people who use vapes?

There aren’t many scientific studies yet with proof about how vaping may impact your health and your vocals. But anecdotally, there are examples of singers who say they are losing vocal range and their tone is being affected after vaping or smoking e-cigarettes. We speak to Cypriot singer and vocal coach Alex Panayi about changes he’s noticed in singers who vape, and Los Angeles-based medical doctor Reena Gupta tells us how it may impact the voice.

summaryZh: 本集 BBC 節目《What in the World》探討電子煙對歌手與發聲器官的影響。節目起因於藝人 Selena Gomez 分享自己長期吸食尼古丁電子煙導致聲音改變並已戒菸的經歷。塞浦路斯歌唱指導 Alex Panayi 與語音專家 Reena Gupta 醫師分析指出，吸食電子煙會使化學物質沉積在呼吸道及聲帶，引發發炎並使聲帶組織變重。這會導致歌手出現聲音疲勞、沙啞與高音音域喪失，且部分損傷可能是永久性的。專家亦探討了演藝者對電子煙產生的心理依賴與成癮問題。
summaryEn: This episode of What in the World explores how vaping nicotine affects singers and their vocal health, sparked by Selena Gomez's recent comments about quitting vaping after it changed her voice. Cypriot vocal coach Alex Panayi and voice specialist Dr. Reena Gupta explain that vaping deposits harmful chemicals in the airways and vocal cords, causing inflammation that can make vocal tissue heavier. This leads to symptoms such as vocal fatigue, raspiness, loss of high range, and potentially permanent vocal damage. The episode also discusses the psychological addiction and pressure surrounding vaping in show business.
